thread:
Sam (Sales): FYI BetaMed POC - customer can't see traces in their Splunk dashboard. Logs show a bunch of 429s coming from our log forwarder. They're getting worried about SLA. Any quick triage?

Priya (SRE): Can you paste an example trace_id or a log snippet? 429s usually mean our drain to their ingest is throttling or creds misconfigured.

Sam (Sales): here's a redacted log we pulled from the customer's forwarding side:

```
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z INFO forwarder sending batch=42 size=128kb sink=splunk-hec status=429 error="rate limit exceeded"
2026-03-18T14:02:11Z WARN forwarder retrying batch=42 attempt=1
2026-03-18T14:02:12Z INFO http request trace_id=ab12cd34ef user=beta-med path=/v1/generate headers={"x-request-id":"rq-0a1b2c","traceparent":"00-ab12cd34ef567890-00f00f00-01"}
```

Sam (Sales): Customer says they can't match trace ids from Console to Splunk. Splunk shows lots of partial traces.

Priya (SRE): Ok - two things to check in parallel: sampling and propagation. If our runtime is dropping spans or issuing sampled=false we won't see full traces in Splunk. Also the forwarder 429s will cause partial ingestion which looks like gaps.

Marco (Solutions Eng): @Sam can you confirm the POC is using our on-prem forwarder (swarm mode) vs direct HEC? If it's on-prem forwarder we've seen buffer saturation when bursts hit 5k rps. Quick mitigation: toggle forwarder.buffered_mode = true and set forwarder.max_concurrency to 8.

Alex (Platform): Also check the Console -> Observability -> Exports page for the export health. If the export() status is "backpressure" it will show a backoff window. If they gave us an S3 role, confirm the trust policy has sts:AssumeRole from our account. Common mistake: role only allows a specific external ID but the customer used a different one.

Priya (SRE): Sam, can you ask them to run this curl from a test client and paste the full response headers?

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <POC_TOKEN>" -H "x-request-id: rq-verify-001" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=xl"
```

Priya (SRE): We want to see if traceparent/request-id are present and propagated by the runtime into the logs. If propagation missing -> fix is config: `tracing.propagation: [traceparent, request-id]` on the runtime group.

Sam (Sales): Customer sent the curl output. Response headers include `x-request-id: rq-verify-001` but Splunk shows events with their own trace ids (not matching) and many events missing traceparent.

Marco (Solutions Eng): That indicates their log ingestion or Splunk HEC pipeline is rewriting or sampling traces. Two suggested checks on their side: 1) confirm HEC `indexerAcknowledgment` is enabled and 2) ensure their pipeline doesn't drop `traceparent`. Also confirm no intermediate proxy (ALB/WAF) is stripping the header.

Alex (Platform): On our side I see recent forwarder logs with backoff windows at the timestamps Sam posted. We probably hit their ingest rate cap. Short term fix: enable retry_with_backoff=true and increase forwarder.buffer_size to 256kb. Long term: recommend they bump HEC ingest quota or we switch to batched S3 export as a fallback.

Sam (Sales): They're asking about timeline and whether this needs infra changes on their side (they're a security team, slow approvals). Any mitigations that avoid them touching infra?

Priya (SRE): If they can't change infra, we can do two things immediately: 1) Turn on our export buffering (client-side buffer) to smooth bursts, 2) Enable prefix-based sampling rules to surface high-value traces so dashboards are useful even with partial ingestion. Both are config toggles we can apply in the POC within 30-60 mins.

Marco (Solutions Eng): I'll prepare a quick runbook for them with the exact Console toggles and commands. Also include these snippets for their Splunk admin:

- Check HEC config: ensure `max_content_length` >= 256kb and `quota` matches expected rps.
- Pipeline rule: keep `traceparent` header as raw field and do not rewrite it.

Priya (SRE): If we still see missing spans after smoothing, we'll need one small test: set `tracing.force_sampling=true` for a 15-minute window so every request emits a full trace (overrides incoming sampling). That will show whether propagation or ingestion is the issue. I'll own that test.

deploy-bot: INFO Deployment queued: change=enable-forwarder-buffering env=beta-med-poc by=Marco ETA=5m

Sam (Sales): Great — Marco do the runbook, Priya do the forced-sample test, Alex coordinate with customer infra on role/trust if they want S3 fallback. I'll update BetaMed and ask for approval to apply buffering.

Priya (SRE): Plan posted. If buffering + forced sampling fixes it we can convert that to a recommended config for Dedicated customers.

Marco (Solutions Eng): Runbook link (private): https://redwood.company/runbooks/poc-splunk-forwarder-buffering (send to BetaMed once cleaned).

Sam (Sales): Thanks team — target: have buffering enabled and first verification (forced sample trace visible in Splunk) within 90 minutes. I'll follow up in this thread with customer permission updates. :thumbsup:
